prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a parking lot collision in Houston, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1460; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim documentation purposes. Can you please state your full name for the record?

A: Sure. I'd prefer to keep my name off the recording, if that's all right. I'm the driver of the blue sedan that was involved in the parking lot incident.

Q: That's fine. We'll refer to you as the claimant. Can you walk me through what happened in the parking lot?

A: I was backing out of a parking space at the shopping center in Houston. I checked my mirrors and didn't see anything, but when I was about halfway out, another vehicle came down the row and hit the rear quarter panel of my car.

Q: Were you moving slowly when the impact occurred?

A: Yes, very slowly. I'd say maybe walking pace. It wasn't a hard hit, but it was enough to jolt me forward and then back against the seat.

Q: Did you notice any injuries right away?

A: Not immediately. I felt a little stiff, but I thought it would pass. By the next morning my neck was sore and it hurt to turn my head to the left. Now I have a dull ache at the base of my skull and my shoulders feel tight.

Q: Have you sought medical treatment since the collision?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic and was diagnosed with a neck strain. I've been doing physical therapy twice a week and taking over-the-counter pain relievers.

Q: Thank you for that. Is there anything else you'd like to add about the incident or your injuries?

A: Just that I'm trying to get back to normal, and I'd appreciate knowing what the next steps are for my vehicle repair and medical coverage.

Q: Absolutely. I'll go over those with you at the end of this call. Thank you for your cooperation.
